outcome: Efficacy (avoiding obstetric hysterectomy and major complications)
cohort: The study included 100 patients with atonic primary postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) who underwent Lower Segment Caesarean Section (LSCS) and did not respond to primary medical management.
finding: Both Bilateral Uterine Artery Ligation (BUAL) and B-lynch sutures were found to be simple, safe, and effective methods for controlling primary PPH during caesarean section due to uterine atony, with success rates of 94% and 96% respectively, and no statistically significant difference in mean blood loss.
mod_finding: The study focused exclusively on primary PPH following Lower Segment Caesarean Section (LSCS), comparing two surgical techniques used during this mode of birth, rather than comparing different modes of birth.
gest_age: Gestational age at delivery was matched between groups, but specific ranges or averages are not provided for the babies, only for the mothers at delivery.
